label: Binding compute treaty with verification
summary: A US-China (or broader) treaty placing binding, independently verified limits on frontier training-compute thresholds, modeled loosely on nuclear arms-control verification regimes.

source.quote: Curator-drafted intervention: bundles the family of 'international AI/compute governance treaty' proposals discussed across AI-governance literature (e.g. compute governance and 'CERN for AI' style proposals) into one representative nudge with real verification, not just a communique.

cost.note: Moderate direct cost (verification infrastructure, inspectors, monitoring), but the binding part is a high diplomatic and sovereignty cost: it requires great powers to accept external audits of their frontier training runs.

nudges.evidence: A verified, binding treaty is close to a direct implementation of the 'binding international AI regime' event, so it gets the largest available nudge, with a one-year lag for ratification and stand-up.
Removing the payoff to secretly outracing a rival meaningfully reduces the incentive to cut safety corners, though other competitive pressures (commercial, other states) remain.
